answer.rationale: Immediate competitive threat to SMB base with doubled churn conversations requires rapid, targeted response. memory_73 confirms promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. memory_57 shows referral incentives work well but are better suited for retention of established customers, not acquisition defense. memory_31 and memory_86 address activation lift, not pricing pressure. memory_91 (activation messaging) and memory_44 (enterprise sales assist) are misaligned with the SMB price-sensitivity crisis. A standard_experiment on targeted promotional pricing for at-risk SMB cohorts balances urgency against verification constraints. Risk flagged: promotional pricing may erode margin perception and create price-expectation anchoring, requiring careful time-limit and segment boundaries. However, losing SMB accounts to competitor price cuts represents greater long-term qualified revenue damage. Preserving uncertainty through controlled scope allows learning application without full-cycle validation.
